ascii_only_is_default_law: S026 §31: ASCII-only must NOT be the default. It is the CONTROL.

merges.rule: keep a merge iff both parts and the result survive

tokenizer_closure_bytes.law: S026 §93: complete executable closure counts tokenizer data
tokenizer_closure_bytes.note: These bytes are MODEL_SPECIFIC. They are the vocabulary's physical program, not free. A row prune that rewrites tokenizer.ggml.* must also recount this bucket.

ascii_prune_control.name: Qwen3.8 ASCII-prune CONTROL
ascii_prune_control.predicate: KEEP a row unless its GPT-2-decoded payload is valid UTF-8 containing at least one non-ASCII codepoint. This keeps all 256 byte-fallback tokens, all 276 special/reserved tail rows, ASCII text, and invalid UTF-8 fragments needed for byte composition. It DROPS accented Latin, CJK, Cyrillic, etc.

ascii_prune_control.verdict: CONTROL reproduced (248320 -> 129006). Net-beneficial on pure-ASCII AgentOS domains (code/JSON/shell/paths/structured, ratio=1). NOT net-beneficial on French/multilingual or typographic English: inflation eats a ~5% LM-head that is only ~5% of decode work (§35). ASCII-only is therefore a measured CONTROL, not the default (§31).

script_cold_prune_candidate.name: script-cold deletion (CJK/Cyrillic/Arabic/Hangul/Thai/…)
script_cold_prune_candidate.why_better_than_ascii_only: Keeps accented Latin, typographic punctuation, and Greek/math symbols so French and curly-quoted English do not inflate. Still a DELETION of cold-script generation rows — input remains representable via byte-fallback, generation capability is NOT proven preserved (§109).

proposed_scheme.why_not_ascii_only: ASCII-only deletes French/Latin-extended generation rows and typographic punctuation used in real English. On this box the LM head is ~5% of decode work, so any inflation ≳ 5% loses. Tool/JSON/code/path/schema tokens are ASCII and do not need that deletion to be cheap. §31, §82, §109.
proposed_scheme.why_not_hot_only_deletion: A 4–6k AgentOS-observed HOT set, used as a DELETE keep-set, inflates even ASCII English (unseen subwords fall to bytes). That is §35 in miniature. HOT is a residency tier, not a deletion whitelist.
protects: JSON structural tokens and JSON Schema keywords
code / shell punctuation and identifiers observed in AgentOS
all 33 added tokens including chat/tool/FIM specials

hot.definition: Always-resident LM-head rows: byte alphabet, added/special tail, AgentOS-observed tokens, protected tool/JSON/code/path/schema surfaces.

warm.definition: Latin/ASCII/Greek/math/symbol rows not in HOT. Stay on the parent disk. Page into the GEMV when the session needs them (accented French, typographic quotes, Δ/≈). Do NOT delete: generation capability lives in these rows (§109).

cold.definition: CJK/Cyrillic/Arabic/Hangul/Thai/… rows. Input still encodes via byte-fallback (3 bytes/char typical). Generation of these tokens requires a page-in of the rows; byte-fallback representability is NOT a proof that generation capability survives (§109). Default is page-in-on-demand, not deletion.
cold.deletion_would_be: the script-cold candidate above; not default

proposed_scheme.two_stage_head: Decode GEMV over HOT every token (~5k–8k rows, ~3% of the full head, ~0.15% of decode FLOPs). WARM/COLD rows exist as a gather-able residual table, scored only on page-in. This removes work from EVERY decode step (§36) WITHOUT the inflation of deleting unseen English subwords.

laws.\u00a730_38: Vocabulary is first-class; VocabularyGenome lives here.
laws.\u00a731: ASCII-only is the CONTROL, not the default.
laws.\u00a735: A 10% smaller LM head that produces 25% more tokens LOSES.
laws.\u00a736: LM head work is on EVERY decode step; high EV only if inflation does not eat it.
laws.\u00a781: Profile real AgentOS token distribution, not generic frequency.
laws.\u00a7109: Free capability != free information. Byte-fallback preserves representability, not generation.
laws.\u00a7118: Tokenizer topology is part of the physical program.
